sources.title: Market Cap Explained
sources.finding: Describes variable conventions: micro below USD250m, small USD250m–2b, mid USD2b–10b, large USD10b–200b, mega USD200b+. The proposed half-open boundaries and merging mega into large are this policy's choices.

sources.title: S&P U.S. Indices Methodology
sources.finding: Currently served document uses company-level addition thresholds USD22.7b, USD8.0b and USD1.2b; it also discusses quarterly review, share classes and separate float requirements. Membership is not a universal size label.
sources.currentness_limit: The live methodology article's Download linked to this July2026 PDF on2026-10-09; no future threshold update is assumed.

sources.title: Global Investable Market Indexes Methodology
sources.finding: Ranks companies by full capitalization and uses cumulative free-float coverage targets with global size bounds. This is not issuer-count quartiles. Multiple securities of a company share a size segment.
sources.currentness_limit: The live latest/GIMI route failed; May full methodology was cross-checked against the July summary linked from the current methodology index.

sources.title: Global Investable Market Indexes Methodology Summary
sources.locator: Index maintenance overview and pp.11–12; current index links summary
sources.finding: Supports the distinction between market coverage, global size requirements and maintenance buffers. It does not prescribe the diagnostic count bands recommended here.

sources.title: S&P/TSX Canadian Indices Methodology
sources.finding: Composite and SmallCap have different universes; capped sector indices generally start with Composite membership and GICS categories. These are index perimeters, not a national issuer census. Index weighting is not full issuer capitalization.

sources.title: S&P/TSX Venture Health Care (Sector) Index
sources.finding: The issuer explicitly defines this as the healthcare subset of its Venture Composite micro-cap universe. This supports a separate perimeter route, not a measured count of eligible WP02 issuers.
sources.limitation: Search-rendered market-cap statistics lacked adequately bound units/as-of and were not used.

sources.title: Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) Methodology
sources.locator: Classification, printed p.3; structure and review
sources.finding: Uses principal business activity with revenue, earnings and review considerations; companies receive one hierarchical assignment. Its exact decision rules differ from the proposed strict-majority fallback. Public methodology is not evidence of a company's classification or a data license.

sources.title: The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, SP800-145
sources.finding: Distinguishes SaaS, PaaS and IaaS. Restricting this pilot's cloud operator scope to externally sold IaaS/PaaS is a research choice, not a NIST sector classification.

sources.title: Euro foreign exchange reference rates
sources.locator: Introduction and quote-basis statement, lines 35–41; history links
sources.finding: Quotes currencies against EUR; publishes reference rates on working days, ordinarily around16:00CET, for information rather than transactions. No rate values from the current page are used as the proposed historical valuation rates.

sources.title: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs)
sources.finding: An ADR can represent multiple underlying ordinary shares or a fraction. Ratio adjustment is therefore required; depositary receipts cannot be counted again on top of the underlying ordinary shares.

sources.title: National Securities Exchanges
sources.finding: Provides a regulator venue-status route. Exchange registration alone does not prove that a security is an operating issuer's primary ordinary-equity listing.
sources.limitation: Page shows an old display date alongside updated venue names; do not treat display date as historical validity of every entry.

sources.title: Recognized exchanges
sources.finding: Navigation route to recognized Canadian exchanges, including CSE and Cboe Canada. Direct open failed; no full register or complete venue inventory is asserted.

sources.title: EU countries
sources.finding: Supports EU27 rather than all of Europe or the EEA. The proposed frozen ISO set is explicit in the policy.

sources.title: Understanding requirements and risks relating to overseas issuers
sources.finding: Confirms that those listing statuses are distinct. The proposed hash assignment resolves a sampling slot only; it cannot establish or change a legal listing status.

sources.title: ESMA Registers help
sources.finding: Official navigation for EU venue status. No venue export, historical admission status or constituent data was acquired.

sources.title: List of licensed (registered) Financial Institutions
sources.finding: Navigation only. An attempted direct exchange PDF failed; no verified full Japanese venue table is claimed.

sources.title: Aquis Stock Exchange Limited register entry
sources.finding: Illustrates the regulator venue-status route beyond the main London market. Direct body was minimal; not a complete UK venue census or historical eligibility proof.

sources.title: Countries in the EU and EEA
sources.finding: Provides the complete EU27 list and distinguishes the additional EEA countries and Switzerland. Used to validate the proposed explicit ISO set.

sources.title: GICS Methodology, live latest route
sources.finding: Codes are compatibility hints for a future entitled issuer-level classification, not an assignment for any company. Live full open failed; the April S&P-hosted methodology supplies the classification-method discussion.
